background.text: No, not at all. I mean, it's a top-down. That's what it is. It isn't right and left. The real issue is who has the power and who doesn't. And I'm contending and can document that voters, workers, consumers, and taxpayers don't have much power at all. It's in the hands of these big companies who are connected with the two parties, fund the same two parties with the same corporate interests, things that John McCain criticized, things that Bill Bradley criticized, even things that Ross Perot criticized. They got millions of votes, but there's no one carrying that torch to November except the Nader-Leduc Green Party ticket.

background.speaker: [target]
background.text: Well, public funding and public campaigns, same-day voter registration, will give voters more voice and won't have their votes nullified by money in politics. That's one. Second, repeal Taft-Hartley Act and other restrictive labor laws that keep tens of millions of workers from forming trade unions, especially those in low-paid jobs, of which there are a huge number. One out of every three workers in this country doesn't earn a living wage. Places like Walmart and McDonald's and Burger King and Kmart. Third, give people universal health insurance. That will sure help consumers. And give consumers some good old-fashioned law enforcement against the corporate crooks and the defrauders, especially which eat away at low-income people in the ghettos, predatory lending. And then finally, taxpayers. Hundreds of billions of dollars going into corporate welfare. Subsidies, giveaways, handouts, the whole works. Give me the worst as you see it.

ground_truth: In terms of these handouts, okay, 1872 Mining Act, never discussed by Bush and Gore, it allows a foreign or domestic corporation to go on our lands, on the federal lands, discover gold, molybdenum, copper, silver, you name it, hard rock metals, they document it with their geologists, they then fly to Washington, the Department of Interior, and Washington, because of this law, has to sell the acreage above the mine for five bucks an acre. So a Canadian company, a few years ago, goes on federal land in Nevada, discovers $9 billion worth of gold, and gets it for $30,000. No royalties back to the government. We're the only country in the world who gives away our natural resources. The other outrage is the drug companies. I would think American companies would be outraged by that. Well, you know, American companies, foreign companies, what's the difference anymore, right? They're all mixed. The other one is the drug companies. They get all this free medicine that's developed. By the taxpayers, the National Institutes of Health, like the anti-cancer drug Taxol or AZT and AIDS, and under our federal government, we give them away the drugs, we give the drugs away to Bristol-Myers Squibb and other companies. No royalties back to the government, no control of drug prices to millions of people. A few months ago, a woman with ovarian cancer said she lost her $19,000 a year job, goes to a doctor, says, very serious, the only drug I can prescribe is Taxol. She says, how much? He said, six treatments. $14,000. Bristol-Myers Squibb didn't spend a cent discovering and human clinically testing that drug. That was done by the taxpayer at the U.S. government, and that's what the story is in drug after drug.

ground_truth: Forced progressive taxation laws against corporations. The New York Times has documented, again, all these shelters and loopholes, and they're increasing and draining away revenues from the government. That could be used for neighborhood and community needs. And look, America needs repair. You know, public transit, schools, clinics, drinking water systems, crumbling, lack of repair. The second is, I don't know if this surplus is going to materialize, Charlie. I mean, this is a projection. I think that both candidates are creating an unnecessary scare on Social Security. Social Security is not in trouble, not in trouble at all. The Social Security trustees say that up all the way to 2037, every dollar will be paid on 1.7% annual growth predictions. We're growing over 4%.
